podcast.title: More Premium Isn't a Brief

lines.speaker: caddie
lines.text: You started with Morning Table and told the AI to make it look premium. You said it three more times after that. When I asked you, "What is your new dessert — flavor, size, what makes it different?" you changed course.

lines.speaker: guest
lines.text: I run a bakery too and I do not have time to write briefs. Why not just say premium? It is faster and costs me nothing to try.

lines.speaker: caddie
lines.text: You tried that with "Make it more premium." and "Still not premium enough. Make it more premium." You got darker backgrounds and fancier fonts, but you still had no product, no price, no reader.

lines.speaker: guest
lines.text: But those drafts helped me see what I do not want. Is that not useful? Writing audience and price up front feels slow when I am still testing.

lines.speaker: caddie
lines.text: That objection holds for early testing, and saying "Even more premium, please." is cheap for direction. I withdraw the full brief for that stage. Use it only when you need a poster customers can act on.

lines.speaker: guest
lines.text: So when did it stop working for you? My supplier keeps telling me premium means gold and black. My customers just want breakfast.

lines.speaker: caddie
lines.text: It stopped when you needed office workers to buy. You wrote the brief for this fictional café demo with audience, mood, and price. When I stayed quiet after that, it was because the poster matched.

lines.speaker: guest
lines.text: What did you actually write? Give me the exact line, not theory.

lines.speaker: caddie
lines.text: You wrote, "The new dessert is matcha basque cheesecake, priced at KRW 6,500." You added office workers near Seongsu station. You named calm, warm morning with soft cream and muted green.

lines.speaker: guest
lines.text: I still have no real photo. A photographer costs money I do not have. Does that kill the brief?

lines.speaker: caddie
lines.text: No, you kept the condition clear. You said you have no real product photo yet and to use a concept illustration. You told it to label it "CONCEPT IMAGE" and make name and price easy to read.

lines.speaker: guest
lines.text: So I can say premium to explore, then I must name product, price, audience, mood to sell? And I admit the photo gap?

lines.speaker: caddie
lines.text: Yes, you use vague words to test speed. You switch to audience, price, mood, and product detail when money is on the line. You keep the concept label until you have a real photo.

manual.title: Poster Brief First for Cafe Desserts
manual.whenToUse: When you ask AI to make a poster for a fictional cafe dessert.
manual.whenNotToUse: When you are only testing art styles with no fixed product or price.

steps.text: State who the poster is for and where they will see it.
steps.check: Checks audience is specific, not a vague style word.

steps.text: Give dessert name and difference, price, and one feeling with colors.
steps.check: Checks product, price, and mood are all present.

steps.text: Say if you have a real photo or need labeled concept illustration.
steps.check: Checks image source and label rule are clear.

steps.text: Make one draft with readable name and price, then wait for revision.
steps.check: Checks name, price, and label match your brief.

pitfalls: Starting with "Make it look premium." with no audience or product.
Repeating "Make it more premium." without adding details.
Giving product details only after you are asked what it is.
Approving style drafts before price and readability are set.
forYourAI: Ask for audience, product detail, price, mood, and photo status before you design.
Do not revise on vague words alone; ask for missing brief details.
If no real photo exists, use concept illustration labeled CONCEPT IMAGE.
Keep product name and price easy to read in the layout.
youDecide: Who the poster is for and where they see it.
Exact dessert name, flavor, and what makes it different.
Price to show and one feeling with colors.
Whether you have a real photo or use labeled concept image.

short.title: Why 'More Premium' Did Not Work

scenes.narration: What happens when you ask for premium three times without a brief?
You told the AI to make it more premium, and you got another luxury poster with no dessert name or price.
Then you wrote, "The new dessert is matcha basque cheesecake, priced at KRW 6,500." The poster changed to show that product and price.
Premium gave the AI no target, so it repeated luxury styles until you named audience, product, and price.
When you want a poster that sells, name audience, product, price, and mood, and label it concept if you have no photo.
Next time you want something premium, what brief will you write first?

card.text: Before you make a café poster, ask me audience, product detail, price, mood, and if I have a real photo.
